headline: Federer wins his 20th Grand Slam title
text: Roger Federer won the Australian Open again, the first man to win 20 Grand Slam singles titles. He is 36.
imageCaption: Roger Federer

headline: eBay replaces PayPal with Adyen
text: On January 31 eBay announced that it will replace PayPal as its main payment processor with the Dutch company Adyen, lowering its costs and giving it more control over payments.
imageCaption: Adyen's office in Amsterdam

headline: A surprise insurance charge at GE Capital
text: General Electric took a charge of about 0.91 dollars a share to top up reserves for old long-term care insurance policies it stopped writing more than a decade ago, and suspended dividends from GE Capital to the parent. Regulators require it to put billions into the insurance business over several years.
source: https://www.annualreports.com/HostedData/AnnualReportArchive/g/NYSE_GE_2017.pdf (GE 2017 annual report letter, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Electric (read 2026-10-03, $14.5 billion required by the Kansas regulator over seven years). The charge was announced in January 2018 with fourth-quarter results; exact date not re-confirmed.
imageCaption: The General Electric Building at 570 Lexington Avenue, New York

headline: IBM's revenue grows again
text: On 18 January IBM reported fourth-quarter revenue of 22.5 billion dollars, up 4% (1% at constant currencies), and said its 'strategic imperatives' such as cloud and analytics now make up 46% of revenue. It took a one-time charge of 5.5 billion dollars for the US tax reform.
imageCaption: The IBM Building in Chicago

headline: Meltdown and Spectre: a security flaw in Intel's processors
text: Researchers reported two security flaws, named Meltdown and Spectre, that affect almost all Intel processors made since 1995 and can let programs read data they should not see. Software fixes are being rolled out.
imageCaption: An Intel Core i7 processor of the generation affected by Meltdown and Spectre

headline: Best sales growth in six years
text: McDonald's reported on 30 January that 2017 brought its best sales growth at existing restaurants in six years, with more customer visits in all segments; fourth-quarter comparable sales rose 5.5%. Revenue fell because McDonald's is selling company-run restaurants to franchisees, which leaves it with fees and rent instead.
imageCaption: Self-order kiosks with card readers at a McDonald's, 2018

headline: US fracking boom lifts revenue, write-offs hit profit
text: Schlumberger reported on 19 January that its 2017 revenue rose 9 percent to 30.4 billion dollars, with a full year of Cameron. Its North American land activity grew 82 percent, in line with the rig count. Fourth-quarter charges of 2.11 dollars a share turned the quarter into a loss. US crude averaged more than 60 dollars in January, the highest monthly average since 2014.
imageCaption: Hydraulic fracturing at a well in North Dakota

headline: Volatility returns: the Dow falls 1,175 points in a day
text: A bigger-than-expected rise in wages in the January jobs report raised fears of inflation and faster rate rises. On 5 February the Dow fell 1,175 points or 4.6%, its largest point drop ever, and the VIX volatility index jumped to its highest since 2015 as bets on calm markets unwound; on 8 February the Dow fell another 1,033 points. The S&P 500 lost 4% in February.
imageCaption: A trader at the closing bell of the New York Stock Exchange on the day the Dow fell 1,175 points, 5 February 2018
imageCredit: Photo by BRYAN R. SMITH/AFP via Getty Images

headline: Now Walmart Inc., the shares slide on slower online growth
text: From 1 February the company is called Walmart Inc. instead of Wal-Mart Stores. On 20 February its shares fell about 10% after holiday-quarter profit came in below forecasts (1.33 dollars a share against 1.36 expected) and US online sales grew 23%, after 50% the quarter before.
imageCaption: A Walmart sign ;;

headline: Woods's first year: a tax windfall hides a flat quarter
text: ExxonMobil reported on 2 February that it earned 19.71 billion dollars in 2017, the first year under Darren Woods, who took over on 1 January 2017 when Rex Tillerson left to become Secretary of State. But 5.9 billion of the total came from the new US tax law; without it and impairments, fourth-quarter profit was 3.73 billion, slightly lower than a year earlier. The company reported a sixth oil discovery off Guyana.
source: ExxonMobil press release of 2 February 2018, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408818000006/f8k4q991.htm (read 2026-10-03); ExxonMobil Form 8-K of 16 December 2016 (Woods from 1 January 2017), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408816000103/0000034088-16-000103.txt (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rex_Tillerson (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The former ExxonMobil Building in Houston

headline: Amazon's sales jump 38% in the holiday quarter
text: Amazon reported fourth-quarter sales of $60.5 billion, up 38%, and net income of $1.9 billion. Sales for 2017 rose 31% to $177.9 billion.
imageCaption: The Spheres at Amazon's headquarters in Seattle

headline: Geely's founder becomes Daimler's biggest shareholder
text: Li Shufu, founder of the Chinese car maker Geely, which owns Volvo, has bought 9.69% of Daimler, making him the largest single shareholder.
imageCaption: Li Shufu, the founder of Geely

headline: Narasimhan takes over and apologises for Cohen payments
text: Vasant Narasimhan became chief executive on 1 February. Within weeks he apologised to employees after it emerged that Novartis had signed a $1.2 million one-year contract with the consulting firm of Michael Cohen, the personal lawyer of President Trump.
imageCaption: Vas Narasimhan, chief executive of Novartis

headline: Production hell, a fatal crash and a big recall
text: Tesla is far behind its targets for Model 3 production, and heavy spending on automated factories is draining its cash; it is one of the most shorted shares on the market. In March a Model X driver was killed in a crash while using Autopilot, and on 29 March Tesla recalled 123,000 older Model S cars over corroding power-steering bolts.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (production hell, March 2018 crash, recall of 29 March 2018, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Tesla cars outside the Tesla factory, Fremont, California

headline: The Finnish state buys a stake in Nokia
text: Solidium, the investment arm of the Finnish government, bought a 3.3% stake in Nokia worth 844 million euros. In January Nokia signed a deal to supply 5G base stations to Japan's NTT Docomo.
imageCaption: The Keilaniemi waterfront in Espoo, where Nokia House stands

headline: Siemens Healthineers goes public
text: Siemens listed its medical technology business, Siemens Healthineers, on the Frankfurt stock exchange on 16 March, selling a 15% stake at 28 euros a share. The flotation was billed as Germany's largest since Deutsche Telekom's in 1996.
imageCaption: A Siemens Healthineers site in Frimley, England

headline: Kenichiro Yoshida succeeds Hirai
text: Kazuo Hirai handed over as chief executive in April and became chairman; his successor is Kenichiro Yoshida, who had led Sony's internet provider So-net and taken it public in 2005.
imageCaption: Kenichiro Yoshida, Sony's chief executive

headline: Trump pulls out of the nuclear deal
text: On 8 May President Trump announced that the United States is leaving the nuclear deal, calling it 'a horrible one-sided deal', and will reimpose sanctions in two stages, in August and November, including on foreign companies that keep trading with Iran. Siemens chief Joe Kaeser said his company cannot take new orders from Iran. Boeing's licences to sell planes to Iran are to be revoked. The European Union and China criticised the decision.
imageCaption: President Trump announces that the United States leaves the nuclear deal with Iran, White House, 8 May 2018

headline: Howard Willard takes over at Altria
text: Howard Willard, a 25-year company veteran who has been chief operating officer and finance chief, succeeded Marty Barrington as chairman and chief executive on 17 May. Altria expects adjusted earnings per share to grow 15 to 19% in 2018, helped by the US tax cut, and raised its share buyback to 2 billion dollars; the quarterly dividend is 70 cents.
imageCaption: The Altria Theater in Richmond, Virginia, Altria's home town

headline: Nestlé pays Starbucks $7.15 billion to sell its coffee
text: Nestlé agreed to pay Starbucks $7.15 billion in a distribution deal for Starbucks coffee products. It adds a big brand to Nescafé and Nespresso.
imageCaption: A cup of Nescafé

headline: Walmart pays 16 billion dollars for India's Flipkart
text: On 9 May Walmart agreed to buy 77% of Flipkart, India's largest online retailer, for 16 billion dollars, beating Amazon to the deal. It is the biggest acquisition in Walmart's history.
imageCaption: A Walmart-owned Best Price wholesale store, Hyderabad, India

headline: The 'eagle' goals against Serbia
text: At the World Cup in Russia, Switzerland drew 1-1 with Brazil and beat Serbia 2-1 with a late goal by Xherdan Shaqiri. Shaqiri and Granit Xhaka, both of Albanian descent, celebrated their goals with a double-headed eagle gesture, the Albanian emblem, which caused a controversy; FIFA did not ban them.
imageCaption: Xherdan Shaqiri at the World Cup in Russia, June 2018

headline: GE is dropped from the Dow after 111 years
text: General Electric was removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average on 26 June and replaced by Walgreens Boots Alliance. It had been in the index continuously since 1907, the longest of any company, and was its worst performer, down more than 55% in a year.
imageCaption: The trading floor of the New York Stock Exchange

headline: Krzanich resigns
text: Chief executive Brian Krzanich resigned with immediate effect on 21 June after an investigation found a past consensual relationship with an employee, against company rules. Finance chief Bob Swan is interim chief executive. Intel is also struggling to start production of its 10-nanometre chips, which are years late.
imageCaption: Brian Krzanich, Intel's chief executive

headline: Microsoft buys GitHub for 7.5 billion dollars
text: On 4 June Microsoft agreed to buy GitHub, the platform where more than 28 million software developers share and work on code, for 7.5 billion dollars.
imageCaption: GitHub's letterbox at its Amsterdam office

headline: The US-China trade war begins
text: On 6 July the US put tariffs on $34 billion of Chinese imports, and China answered in kind. President Trump started the dispute in March, citing unfair trade practices and theft of intellectual property, and threatens tariffs on far more.
imageCaption: President Trump with Chinese Vice Premier Liu He, 2018

headline: US subpoena over bribery
text: On 3 July Glencore said the US Department of Justice had subpoenaed documents on its compliance with the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and money-laundering laws, covering its business in Nigeria, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Venezuela since 2007. Copper fell 10% and zinc 14% in July.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glencore (Investigation by U.S. Department of Justice, citing Glencore's statement); World Bank Pink Sheet monthly averages (both read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building (photograph from 2026)

headline: Berkshire loosens its rules for buying back its own shares
text: On 17 July Berkshire's board scrapped the rule that it may buy back shares only at no more than 20% above book value. Now repurchases can be made whenever Buffett and Munger believe the price is below Berkshire's intrinsic value, as long as cash stays above 20 billion dollars.
imageCaption: Kiewit Plaza in Omaha, home of Berkshire Hathaway's head office

headline: Cisco posts record quarterly revenue
text: Cisco reported record quarterly revenue of $12.8 billion, up 6%, and fiscal-year revenue of $49.3 billion, up 3%. Net income for the year was only $0.1 billion because of a $10.4 billion charge related to the new US tax law. It forecasts growth of 5% to 7% for the next quarter.
imageCaption: Chuck Robbins, Cisco's chief executive, April 2018
imageCredit: Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff from Washington D.C, United States

headline: The first trillion-dollar company
text: On 2 August Apple became the first US listed company to be worth one trillion dollars.
imageCaption: Apple Park, Apple's new headquarters in Cupertino

headline: Coca-Cola buys Costa Coffee
text: On 31 August Coca-Cola agreed to buy the British coffee chain Costa from Whitbread for 3.9 billion pounds. Costa runs coffee shops in Britain and other countries.
imageCaption: A Costa coffee shop in England

headline: 'Funding secured': Musk tweets about taking Tesla private
text: On 7 August Elon Musk wrote on Twitter that he was considering taking Tesla private at 420 dollars a share and that 'funding' was 'secured'. The shares jumped, then fell back as doubts grew about whether the money was really lined up.
imageCaption: Elon Musk, chief executive of Tesla, July 2018

headline: Musk settles with the SEC and loses the chairmanship
text: Musk settled securities-fraud charges brought by the SEC over his 'funding secured' statements: he pays a 20 million dollar fine, gives up the chairmanship of Tesla, and his tweets will be reviewed by Tesla's lawyers; two independent directors join the board.
imageCaption: Robyn Denholm, who became Tesla's chair, May 2018

headline: A surprise profit: 'a truly historic quarter'
text: Tesla reported a third-quarter profit of 312 million dollars and free cash flow of 881 million on 24 October, with a gross margin above 20% on the Model 3. It expects to stay profitable in the fourth quarter.
imageCaption: Tesla Model 3 (photograph from 2024)

headline: Revenue disappoints, then IBM buys Red Hat for 34 billion dollars
text: IBM's third-quarter revenue of 18.76 billion dollars missed forecasts of 19.1 billion and the shares fell 7.6% on 17 October, adding to a falling market. On 28 October IBM agreed to buy Red Hat, the open-source software company, for 34 billion dollars, its biggest acquisition ever, to catch up with Amazon and Microsoft in cloud computing.
imageCaption: Ginni Rometty, IBM's chairman and chief executive

headline: A new 737 MAX crashes in Indonesia
text: On 29 October a Lion Air Boeing 737 MAX 8 crashed after take-off from Jakarta, killing all 189 people on board. The MAX is the newest version of Boeing's best-selling jet and has been in service for little more than a year.
imageCaption: A Lion Air Boeing 737 MAX 8, registration PK-LQP, the aircraft lost on flight JT610 off Jakarta, 29 October 2018

headline: Flannery out, Culp in; a 22 billion dollar write-off and a one-cent dividend
text: On 1 October General Electric replaced John Flannery with board member Larry Culp, former head of Danaher and the first outsider to run GE. On 30 October it reported a third-quarter loss of 22.8 billion dollars, mostly a write-off on the power business, and cut the quarterly dividend from 12 cents to 1 cent.
imageCaption: Larry Culp, the former Danaher chief named General Electric's chairman and chief executive on 1 October 2018
imageCredit: rights holder not named (portrait published by CNBC at his appointment)

headline: The crypto hangover
text: On 15 November Nvidia reported record data-centre revenue but said its near-term results reflect excess inventory of graphics cards left over after the cryptocurrency boom, when miners bought them in large numbers, and gave a weak forecast. Chief executive Jensen Huang said the problem will be corrected.
imageCaption: A cryptocurrency mining rig built from graphics cards

headline: Oil slumps 40% in three months
text: Brent fell from $86 in early October to about $50 at the end of December, and US crude to about $45, while US crude output reached new records near 12 million barrels a day.
imageCaption: An oil tanker in New York harbour, January 2018

headline: Trade truce, then Huawei's finance chief is arrested
text: At the G20 summit on 1 December the US and China agreed a 90-day pause in new tariffs. The same day Canada arrested Meng Wanzhou, Huawei's chief financial officer, at the request of the US, which became known a few days later. US tariffs of 10% have applied to $200 billion of Chinese goods since September.
imageCaption: The US and Chinese delegations at the G20 dinner, Buenos Aires, 1 December 2018

headline: The Christmas fall: shares lose 9 percent in December
text: Worries about the trade war with China and slowing world growth, a Fed rate rise on 19 December that investors felt ignored the tightening in markets, and a partial government shutdown sent shares down hard. By Christmas Eve the S&P 500 stood at 2,351, nearly 20% below its September record, before the Dow jumped 1,086 points on 26 December. The S&P 500 lost 9% in December to 2,506.85 and 6% in 2018, its worst year since 2008; the Dow fell 5.6%. It was the Fed's fourth rise of the year, to 2.25 to 2.5 percent, and December was the S&P 500's worst month since February 2009. The numbers: the Fed's rate 2.25 to 2.5 percent. Inflation 2.2 percent. Unemployment 3.8 percent.
source: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20181219.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20190130.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_stock_market_crashes_and_bear_markets (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_daily_changes_in_the_Dow_Jones_Industrial_Average (read 2026-10-03); data/reference/sp500.json; https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20181219a.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GS10 (read 2026-10-03); https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FEDFUNDS, DFEDTAR, DFEDTARL, DFEDTARU, CPIAUCNS and UNRATE (downloaded 2026-10-04)
imageCaption: The Fed's interest rate (blue), inflation (red) and unemployment (grey) in the United States, 1955 to December 2018
imageCredit: Chart: Month by Month. Data: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

headline: Altria invests 12.8 billion dollars in Juul
text: On 20 December Altria bought 35% of Juul Labs, the leading US e-cigarette maker, for 12.8 billion dollars, valuing Juul at 38 billion. It is the biggest investment in Altria's history; CEO Howard Willard says adult smokers will increasingly choose non-combustible products. Earlier in December Altria agreed to buy 45% of the Canadian cannabis company Cronos for 1.8 billion dollars. Juul is under fire for the popularity of its products among teenagers.
imageCaption: A Juul e-cigarette with flavour pods ;;

headline: Novartis buys AveXis for gene therapy
text: This year Novartis bought AveXis, a developer of gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, for $218 a share, $8.7 billion in total. Novartis also sold its stake in the consumer health joint venture to GlaxoSmithKline for $13 billion in March.
imageCaption: Novartis buildings in Basel
